_comment: The product's own charter -- the palette a duplicate builds with when it has not chosen one yet. Same shape as `data/brand.json` and read by the same reader (`tools/convener_ops/brand.py`), which takes this file whenever no `data/brand.json` exists. An instance never edits this; it writes its own values in `data/brand.json` instead, and `config/boundary.yml` hands that directory to the instance so upstream never touches it back.
_why_a_default: So that a duplicate looks finished at its first build rather than grey. The objection this project already paid for once is D-16: an *invented* palette that measured worse than the one it replaced, and cost accessibility for months because nobody rechecked the numbers. The parade is below and in `scripts/generate_brand_css.py`: every pairing in `contrast` is recomputed from the two colours beside it at every run of `--check`, and a pairing under 4.5 stops the build. A default that cannot clear AA does not ship.
_no_motif: There is deliberately no `motif` section here, and its absence is the decision rather than an omission. `motif` is the ribbon's stroke and the logo's dots -- what somebody drew, and what people recognise. A default one would be worn by every duplicate that forgot to configure a mark, so `tools/convener_ops/brand.py::motif` refuses instead, naming what is missing and where to put it. A default that leaks when you forget it is not a default, it is a trap.
_source: brand/convener/README.md -- the product's mark, and the two colours measured off the original artwork: navy #012765 and coral #fd6b52. Those two are the only values here that were measured rather than derived; everything else below is worked out from them by the rule in `derived._derivation`.
_names: The keys are the system's, not this palette's: `purple` names the role the dominant ink plays (headlines, ribbon, wordmark), `turquoise` the role the saturated field plays, `cream` the bands laid across it. They are inherited from the instance that first measured them, and they are what `scripts/generate_brand_css.py` and both stylesheets already read, so renaming them here would be a second change wearing this one's clothes. Read them as positions in the composition, never as hues -- `purple` is navy here, and `turquoise` is a coral field.

_roles.purple: Headlines, ribbon, wordmark. The dominant colour, not an accent. Navy, measured off the mark: 14.19 on white, AAA with room.
_roles.turquoise: A ground. Never a text colour on white or cream -- 1.61 on white, exactly as unusable there as the other palette's own field. The product's coral, lightened to the field's luminance.
_roles.cream: Full-width horizontal bands laid across the field. Text sits inside them.
_roles.ink: Primary text. Warm, not black -- it carries the palette's own hue rather than being a neutral grey borrowed from nowhere.
_roles.ink_muted: Secondary text. Clears AA on the field and on the bands, which is what decides how light it may be.
_roles.rule: Rules, borders, dividers. Never text -- 1.81 on white.
_roles.black: Body copy on the coloured field, where the composition sets it directly on the ground rather than inside a band.
_roles.white: Inside photographic frames only. Not a ground.

derived._comment: Values no measurement supplies, needed because the web has states and links that a mark does not. Each clears AA on the ground it can appear on.
derived._derivation: One rule, applied to every value here and to four in `colour` above, so that none of them is a taste: **the product's own hues, at the lightness the system measures each role at.** The two measured colours give three axes -- navy for the dominant, coral for the field, and the two in equal parts for the neutrals (they sit near enough to opposite each other that their blend is this palette's own grey, #7f495c). Each token is then its axis mixed toward white or toward black until its WCAG relative luminance matches the luminance that role carries in the charter the system's contrast obligations were written against. That is why nine of the twelve pairings below land within 0.03 of the figure the same pairing gives there; the other three are the ones the navy simply wins (purple_on_turquoise and turquoise_on_purple at +0.89, purple_on_cream at +1.30, white_on_purple at +1.45). A contrast ratio is a function of two luminances, and the luminances were matched on purpose. `purple_hover` is the one exception and says so.
derived._purple_hover: The one value not set by matching a luminance. The dominant's own hover state is barely a luminance step in the charter this rule was taken from (0.0324 to 0.0314), and copying that proportion onto a navy already at 0.0240 would have rounded to the navy itself -- a hover state indistinguishable from its rest state, which is not a state. It is the dominant a fifth of the way to black instead: 15.96 against white, against 14.19 at rest, and it is only ever a filled background (`--purple-d`, `--accent-hover`), never text.
derived._coral: The measured coral #fd6b52 is the source of `turquoise`, `turquoise_tint` and `turquoise_text` and appears raw in none of them, which is not an oversight: at 2.84 on white it can be neither text nor a light ground, and every token in this system is one or the other. It keeps its own role where that role is safe -- the accent on the ink, in the mark itself (`brand/convener/convener-mark.svg`), and in whatever `motif` an instance writes.

contrast._comment: Measured, WCAG 2.1 relative luminance. AA normal text = 4.5, AAA = 7. Recomputed from the colours above by `scripts/generate_brand_css.py` on every run, `--check` or not: a pairing that no longer recomputes, or one that recomputes below 4.5, stops the build rather than being trusted. The twelve pairings are the same twelve the system holds every palette to -- the composition creates them, not this palette.
contrast._forbidden: turquoise as text on white (1.61); rule as text on any ground (1.81 on white); white as text on turquoise (1.61) -- which is why a primary button fills with the dominant, not with the field.

typography._faces: The faces the product itself ships, in `fonts/`, and the ones its own wordmark is drawn in (`brand/convener/README.md`). An instance that names other faces has to ship them the same way.
typography._self_hosted: Not negotiable, and not a preference of this palette's. A webfont request to a third party discloses every visitor's address -- D-17.

layout._ground: The field fills the page. White is not the ground.
layout._bands: Cream bands run the full width, horizontally, across the field. Text sits inside them. They are what give the composition its rhythm -- D-18.
